# W36 · Chat should have an interrupt button

## Summary

A chat on the page now has an Interrupt button, shown while the agent is answering. On a turn the page runs it ends the agent as ctrl-c would; on a chat the terminal screen runs in the background it types Esc, which stops the answer and drops any message still waiting to be typed. The conversation goes on with the next message, an interrupt that arrives just as a turn ends is refused rather than spoiling the next one, and each interrupt is written to the chat's log. The backend is covered by passing tests against stand-in agents; the button's page flow and Esc against a real claude could not be run here (no browser, no claude), so those are unseen.

## Goal

Chat should have an interrupt button

## Tree

### W36.1 · Interrupt a chat's answer in the backend
Status: confirmed
Approach: `chat.py`: `Chats.interrupt(scope)` stops what is answering. A headless page turn (`run_turn`) is tracked per scope and sent SIGTERM then SIGKILL after TURN_GRACE, as a timeout does, and its end is recorded as "Interrupted" rather than as a failure. A background chat (the screen's agent) is sent Esc, which claude takes as "stop this answer" without ending the session: `ptyrelay.Relay.interrupt()` writes `\x1b` to the pty and drops messages still queued to be typed; the walkers (`tui.py`, `walk.py` headless) get `chat_interrupt`. `web.py` gets `POST /api/chat/interrupt {scope}`, refusing when nothing is answering. Each interrupt is written to the chat's log. Check: unit tests in `test_chat.py`, `test_ptyrelay.py`, `test_web.py` (a slow stub turn is stopped and the chat accepts the next message; a fake agent on a pty receives Esc and queued text is dropped).
Determination: An interrupt stops a page-run turn (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and sends Esc to a screen-run chat that is answering, dropping its queued messages; the new tests pass, but Esc was tested against a stand-in agent, not a real claude.

### W36.2 · The button on the page
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: `scripts/web/index.html`: an Interrupt button in the chat form, shown only while `st.busy`, posting `/api/chat/interrupt`; the Send button stays disabled meanwhile. README's chat paragraph gains a line. Check: a flow in `ui_flows.mjs` (playwright, if it runs here) shows the button while busy and none when idle; if no browser starts, say so.
Determination: The chat dialog shows an Interrupt button only while the agent is answering, and it posts to the new interrupt endpoint; the page flow and button are written but unrun here, since there is no browser or node in this environment, so the check that the button appears and works is still owed to a machine with playwright.

### W36.3 · Fix: a late interrupt leaves a stale `stopped` flag that kills the next turn
Parent: W36.1
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py` `Chats.turn`, the end of a turn takes `self.lock` twice: first to read and discard `scope` from `self.stopped` and pop `self.procs`, then (after `chatlog.log`, which does file IO) to pop `self.busy`. `Chats.interrupt` checks `scope in self.busy`, so an interrupt arriving between the two blocks passes the check, adds `scope` to `self.stopped` and returns success, though the turn is already over. Nothing clears that flag; the next `send` for the scope runs a turn whose `track()` sees `scope in self.stopped` and SIGTERMs the new agent at once, which then reports "Interrupted." with no answer. Fix: do the `stopped`/`procs` discard and the `busy` pop in one critical section (or have `interrupt` ignore a turn whose process has finished, and clear `stopped` when a turn begins in `send`). Add a test in `test_chat.py` that interrupts after the turn has read `stopped` but before `busy` is popped (e.g. by patching `chatlog.log` to call `interrupt`) and then checks that the next message is answered normally.
Determination: `Chats.turn` now discards `stopped`/`procs`, saves the session, sets the note and pops `busy` in one critical section, so an interrupt after that point is refused with "nothing is answering" and leaves no stale flag; the new test goes red on the old code and green on the new, and the other chat tests pass apart from the unrelated environmental failure.

- W36.2's flow `chat_interrupt` in `ui_flows.mjs` and the button have never run (no browser here); run them where playwright exists.

Determination: The README now says an interrupted first message leaves no session behind; the failing screen-chat test fails identically on the base commit, so it is environmental; the Hypothesis for W36.1 cannot be added to a node already confirmed, and the button flow still needs a machine with node and playwright, so those two stay unseen.

### W36.5 · Hypothesis: Esc stops a real claude's answer without ending or redirecting the session
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach: W36.1 sends `\x1b` to the pty of a screen-run chat (`ptyrelay.Relay.interrupt`, reached from `Chats.interrupt`) and rests on it that a real claude takes Esc while answering as "stop this answer", keeps the session open and then accepts the next typed message. It was tested only against a stand-in pty agent, and W36.1 has no `Hypothesis:` saying so (it is confirmed, so it cannot be edited). State it as a Hypothesis with its page on this node: the assumption, and that it is refuted if a real claude quits, opens a menu or dialog, ignores Esc, or eats the next message after it; also that Esc is sent only when `typed_at > 0 or active` because Esc twice at an idle prompt opens the rewind menu. If a real claude is available, try it and append the evidence; if not, say it is unseen and leave it for the author.

### W36.6 · Minor findings from the review
Parent: W36.1
Status: open
Approach:
- README (the Interrupt paragraph) says an interrupted first message leaves the page showing only "Interrupted."; the sent message also stays shown because `pending` is cleared only when it reaches a transcript. Reword.
- `Chats.turn`: an interrupt landing after the agent finished normally but before the end-of-turn critical section labels a good answer "Interrupted." (the answer is kept through the session id); harmless, could be noted in a comment.
- `Chats.interrupt` calls `chatlog.log` (file IO) while holding `self.lock`; other holders of the lock wait on it. Log after releasing the lock if easy.
- The `chat_interrupt` flow in `ui_flows.mjs` and the Interrupt button have never run (no node or playwright here); run them where they exist.

# W36 · Chat should have an interrupt button

## Summary

The chat dialog now shows an Interrupt button in place of Send while the agent is answering. It stops a turn the page runs itself, or types one Esc into a chat the terminal screen runs in the background and drops a message not yet typed; the conversation stays, the log shows an "Interrupted." note, and the next message goes on from it. The server side is covered by tests, but the page script and its browser flow could not be run here (no node, playwright or browser), and claude's reaction to the Esc was checked only against its documentation, not a live claude.

## Tree

### W36.1 · Interrupt a turn the page runs itself
Status: confirmed
Approach: In `scripts/chat.py`, `run_turn` reports its `Popen` to the caller, and `Chats` keeps it per scope while the turn runs. New `Chats.interrupt(scope)` stops that process the way a timeout does (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after `TURN_GRACE`), also when the turn's thread has not started the process yet, and raises `ValueError("nothing to interrupt")` when the chat is not answering. The turn's thread then records a note "Interrupted." instead of the agent's exit as a failure, keeps the sent message shown, and frees the chat so the next message resumes the session. `web.py` serves it as `POST /api/chat/interrupt {scope}`. Checked in `test_chat.py` with a stub that sleeps (turn killed, no error text from the exit code, a second send works) and in `test_web.py` (the route, 409 when idle, 403 under `--no-walk`).
Determination: A turn the page runs is stopped by `Chats.interrupt` (also before its agent exists), ends as an "Interrupted." note rather than a failure, and the next message resumes; the new tests and the route test pass, while one older chat test (`exec -a` of the session id) fails here with or without the change.
